newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Office Depot to ramp up openings.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Office Depot to ramp up openings.

text.p: Office Depot Inc Chief Executive David Fuente said on Tuesday his company's $4 billion deal to merge with Staples Inc was dead and that Office Depot would resume its fast pace of expansion by 1998.

Fuente also told Reuters the deal knocked down on Monday by a federal judge would result in a second fiscal quarter charge of $6 million or more to cover fees paid to lawyers and investment bankers arising from the blunted merger.
Office Depot, a leading U.S. operator of office-goods superstores, took a similar $6 million charge against its first-quarter earnings.

Wall Street analysts had forecast that Office Depot earned $0.21 a share in the just-ended second quarter before taking into account charges arising from the failed Staples merger agreed last September.
Fuente said that Office Depot's board of directors were scheduled to meet on Wednesday but were unlikely to vote to appeal Monday's judicial ruling blocking the Staples deal.

The combination of rivals Staples and Office Depot would have created by far the biggest office-supply retailer in the country and was opposed on antitrust grounds by federal regulators and at least eight state governments.
According to analysts, the proposed merger consumed top management's thinking since last September and slowed down the company's fast pace of store openings.

Alex Brown & Sons analyst Christopher Vroom said Office Depot, based in Delray Beach, Florida, had lost several key executives in its development operation since September and may be six months or more behind its plan for opening new stores.
"We would have liked to open 80 stores this year; we will do about 40," Fuente said. "I fully expect to return to our 80- to-100 rate in 1998."
Fuente said Office Depot's finances were sound and had not been hurt by the drawn-out struggle to merge but that rebuilding the company's development operation was a key short-term management task.
Office Depot has $50 million or more in cash and an untapped credit line of $350 million to finance store openings, he said.
Vroom said Office Depot was likely to expand in the northeastern United States, a stronghold of Staples, as well as in southeastern and other markets not yet fully penetrated by the company.
But Fuente said only Philadelphia and Boston in the northeastern United States were attractive to Office Depot and he had no plans to open outlets there any time soon.
Office Depot was most immediately interested in south Florida, Atlanta and smaller markets, he said.
Vroom said Office Depot would need three to six months tonormalize its business and that the shares at 15-1/2, down 3-15/16, were good value at seven times estimated 1997 cash flow.
